# metadata-crawler

> metadata-crawler (CLI: `mdc` or `metadata-crawler`, Python package: `metadata_crawler`) harvests metadata from climate and earth-system datasets on POSIX file systems, S3-compatible object stores, OpenStack Swift and intake catalogues. It normalises the metadata according to a TOML "DRS" configuration, stores it in a source of truth (intake catalogue, MongoDB or PostgreSQL) and indexes it into search systems (Apache Solr, MongoDB). It is part of the Freva ecosystem (freva-org) and released under the BSD license.

Install with `python -m pip install metadata-crawler` or `conda install -c conda-forge metadata-crawler`. Optional dependencies: `pymongo` (MongoDB), `sqlalchemy` and `psycopg` (PostgreSQL), and the `vault` extra (`metadata-crawler[vault]`, pulls in `pyrage`) for age encrypted secrets.

## Core concepts

- Two-stage pipeline: `add` crawls data into a **source of truth** (a permanent store of all metadata), `<index system> index` copies the source of truth into a **search index**. The index can be rebuilt at any time; the source of truth is authoritative.
- Sources of truth: intake catalogues (a YAML file plus gzipped JSONLines data files, local or on S3), MongoDB, PostgreSQL. The backend is derived from the store URL: `mongodb://`/`mongodb+srv://` is MongoDB, `postgresql://`/`postgres://` is PostgreSQL, `.yml`/`.yaml` paths are intake. Override with `--backend`/`-cb` (`intake`, `jsonlines`, `mongodb`, `postgresql`) or `MDC_BACKEND`.
- Versions: metadata is written to two collections, `latest` (only the newest dataset versions) and `files` (all versions).
- The DRS configuration (`drs_config.toml`, option `-c`) defines datasets (where data lives, `fs_type`, `storage_options`), dialects (how to parse paths and file names, e.g. CMIP6, CMIP5, CORDEX ship with the package), a schema of typed facets, and special rules. Dialects and datasets support inheritance and Jinja2 templating.
- Database sources of truth do mark-and-sweep: records not seen in a crawl are removed after a grace period (`--sweep-grace-period`, `MDC_GRACE_DAYS`, default 5 days); disable with `--no-sweep` for partial crawls.
- Named connections: stores can be defined once in `~/.config/metadata-crawler/connections.toml`, with credentials in a separate private `secrets.toml` (optionally age encrypted as `secrets.toml.age`). On the command line a store argument can then be a name (`mdc glance prod`).

## Command line

- `mdc add STORE -c drs_config.toml [-ds DATASET ...] [-d PATH ...]` crawl datasets (`-ds/--data-set`, repeat the flag for several, wildcards allowed) or explicit paths (`-d/--data-object`) into a source of truth.
- `mdc remove STORE -f KEY VALUE [-f KEY VALUE ...] [--dry-run]` delete entries from a source of truth. Same key: OR; different keys: AND. Keys and string values are lower-cased, values may contain `*` and `?`. Unknown keys and time facets are ignored; with no usable facet nothing is removed.
- `mdc glance STORE [--json]` show the metadata (schema, counts, timestamp) of a source of truth.
- `mdc solr index STORE ... --server HOST:PORT [--rotate --min-docs N --configset NAME]` and `mdc mongo index STORE ... --url URL --database DB [--rotate]` index one or more sources of truth (paths, URLs, globs or connection names). `--rotate` builds a fresh index and swaps it in atomically.
- `mdc solr delete ...` / `mdc mongo delete ... -f KEY VALUE` delete from a search index (wildcards supported).
- `mdc config -c drs_config.toml [--json]` print the merged DRS configuration.
- `mdc init-config [--force]` write commented templates of `connections.toml` (mode 0640) and `secrets.toml` (mode 0600).
- `mdc walk-intake CATALOGUE` traverse and print an intake catalogue.
- Store options: `-s/--storage-option KEY VALUE` after the sub-command (repeatable, e.g. `-s username u -s password p`).
- General options, accepted before or after the sub-command: `-v` (repeat for more), `--log-suffix`, `--mdc-config PATH`, `--mdc-secrets PATH`.

## Python API

- `from metadata_crawler import add, remove, index, delete, glance_metadata, get_config, init_config`; async variants: `async_add`, `async_remove`, `async_index`, `async_delete`.
- `add(*config_files, store=..., data_set=[...] | data_object=[...], storage_options={...}, batch_size=..., no_sweep=False)`. Note: `store` is keyword-only; positional arguments are DRS config files.
- `remove(store, facets=[("variable", "tas"), ("project", "cmip6")], dry_run=False, storage_options=None) -> int` returns the number of removed (or, with `dry_run`, matching) entries.
- `index("solr", store, ..., server="localhost:8983")`, `index("mongo", store, ..., url=..., database=...)`; `delete(index_system, facets=[...], **backend_options)`.
- Every `store` argument accepts a path, a URL or a connection object. Names are not resolved in Python; use the configuration explicitly:

```python
from metadata_crawler import add, glance_metadata
from metadata_crawler.api.stores.postgresql import PostgresConnection
from metadata_crawler.connections import read_configfiles

with read_configfiles() as config:                 # reads and decrypts once
    prod = config.get("prod", PostgresConnection)  # raises TypeError for other backends
    add("drs_config.toml", store=prod, data_set="cmip6-fs")
    glance_metadata(config["scratch"])
    staging = config.resolve("prod", db_schema="staging")  # name or URL, with overrides
# secrets are dropped here; using `config` afterwards raises RuntimeError
```

- Ad-hoc connections without files: `MongoConnection.from_url("mongodb://host/db", username="u", password="p")`, likewise `PostgresConnection` (`metadata_crawler.api.stores.postgresql`) and `IntakeConnection` (`metadata_crawler.api.stores.jsonlines`, extra keys are s3fs options).

## Connection files

- `connections.toml`: one table per named store. Keys: `url` (required; `uri` and `path` are synonyms; relative paths are relative to the file), `backend` (optional), `secrets` (optional: name of the secrets table to use), `description`. Backend keys: intake takes s3fs options (`endpoint_url`, `anon`, ...); PostgreSQL takes `host`, `port` (5432), `database` (`metadata`), `db_schema` (`metadata_crawler`) and rejects unknown keys; MongoDB takes `host`, `port`, `database` (`metadata`) and turns every other key into a URI option (`tls`, `replicaSet`, `authSource` defaulting to `admin`).
- `secrets.toml`: tables merged into the connection of the same name (or the one referring to them via `secrets = "table"`). Keys: `username`/`user`, `password`/`passwd`, S3 `key` + `secret` (together) and `token`. Must not be readable by group or others, or it is rejected. Values are masked in logs and never written into catalogue metadata.
- Precedence per key: connections.toml < secrets.toml < `-s` options and `MDC_STORAGE_OPTIONS`.
- File lookup: `--mdc-config` > `MDC_CONFIG_PATH` > `~/.config/metadata-crawler/connections.toml`; `--mdc-secrets` > `MDC_SECRETS_PATH` > `~/.config/metadata-crawler/secrets.toml`. `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` moves `~/.config`. `secrets.toml.age` next to the secrets path is preferred over the plaintext file. Explicitly given files must exist; missing default files count as empty.
- Decryption: identity from `MDC_AGE_IDENTITY` (SSH private key or age key file), else `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, `~/.ssh/id_rsa`; passphrase from `MDC_SECRETS_PASSPHRASE`, else a prompt on a terminal. Passphrase-protected SSH keys are not supported.
- CLI name resolution: an argument is treated as a name only if it has no `scheme://` and is not an existing path; unknown names are passed through unchanged (so `mdc add new.yml` and `mdc glance localhost -cb mongodb` keep working). Names cover metadata stores only, not index server options (`--server`, `--url`) and not dataset `storage_options` in the DRS config (use Jinja2 templating with environment variables there).

## Environment variables

- `MDC_STORAGE_OPTIONS`: comma separated `key:value` pairs, same as `-s`, e.g. `username:u,password:p`.
- `MDC_CONFIG_PATH`, `MDC_SECRETS_PATH`: connections and secrets files.
- `MDC_AGE_IDENTITY`, `MDC_SECRETS_PASSPHRASE`: decrypting `secrets.toml.age`.
- `MDC_BACKEND`: default source-of-truth backend for URLs without a recognisable scheme.
- `MDC_GRACE_DAYS`: sweep grace period in days.
- `DRS_STORAGE_PASSWD`: password for storage backends (`mdc add -p` prompts for it).

- [Usage](https://metadata-crawler.readthedocs.io/en/latest/chapter1-usage/index.html): the two-stage workflow, versions, sweeping
- [Command-line interface](https://metadata-crawler.readthedocs.io/en/latest/chapter1-usage/sec1-cli.html): every sub-command with examples, index rotation, removal semantics
- [Python API](https://metadata-crawler.readthedocs.io/en/latest/chapter1-usage/sec2-python.html): synchronous and asynchronous functions, library reference
- [Named connections and secrets](https://metadata-crawler.readthedocs.io/en/latest/chapter1-usage/sec3-connections.html): connections.toml, secrets.toml, age encryption, precedence, Python usage

## Configuration

- [Configuration overview](https://metadata-crawler.readthedocs.io/en/latest/chapter2-config/index.html): layers of a drs_config.toml
- [Datasets](https://metadata-crawler.readthedocs.io/en/latest/chapter2-config/sec1-datasets.html): root paths, fs_type, storage_options, defaults
- [Dialects](https://metadata-crawler.readthedocs.io/en/latest/chapter2-config/sec2-dialects.html): DRS standards and how paths are parsed
- [Path and data specs](https://metadata-crawler.readthedocs.io/en/latest/chapter2-config/sec3-specs.html): extracting facets from paths and file contents
- [Special rules](https://metadata-crawler.readthedocs.io/en/latest/chapter2-config/sec4-special.html): conditionals and computed facets
- [Schema and field options](https://metadata-crawler.readthedocs.io/en/latest/chapter2-config/sec5-schema.html): facet types such as `string`, `datetime[2]`, `float[4]`, `string[]`
- [Jinja2 templating](https://metadata-crawler.readthedocs.io/en/latest/chapter2-config/sec6-templates.html): templated values, environment variables
- [Inheritance](https://metadata-crawler.readthedocs.io/en/latest/chapter2-config/sec7-inheritance.html): reusing dialects and datasets

## Extending

- [API reference](https://metadata-crawler.readthedocs.io/en/latest/chapter3-api/index.html): plugin entry points (`metadata_crawler.storage_backends`, `metadata_crawler.index_backends`)
- [Storage backends](https://metadata-crawler.readthedocs.io/en/latest/chapter3-api/sec1-storage-backends.html): implementing a `PathTemplate` for a new file system
- [Index backends](https://metadata-crawler.readthedocs.io/en/latest/chapter3-api/sec2-index-backends.html): implementing a new search index
